data.narrative:
Dimensional Energy is a Series A climate and energy company that has raised $25.4M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector includes nine known private peers—among them Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen—alongside one public comparable (Lonza, ticker LNZA). However, a sufficiently narrow peer set at the same stage and valuation tier does not exist to support a reliable peer-median valuation approach; the wider Climate & Energy universe lacks three or more directly comparable Series A transactions.

Given this constraint, the analysis relies on stage-progression methodology. Using the $25.4M in total capital raised as a proxy for post-money value at Series A entry, and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier to project forward valuation progression, this method implies a valuation of $51M.

The triangulated range, supported by a single applicable method, is $43M (low), $51M (median), to $58M (high). The wide spread reflects the methodological limitation: with only stage-progression available and no peer validation, the analysis carries material uncertainty. Key risks to valuation include: (i) absence of comparable Series A financings to validate step-up assumptions; (ii) sector-specific technical and regulatory execution risk; and (iii) potential for a narrower peer set to emerge as additional Climate & Energy companies reach comparable funding milestones. A median estimate of $51M should be treated as preliminary pending access to tighter comparable data.
